hazard: Lack of mandatory sprinkler systems in care homes for limited mobility residents

reports.title: Daphne Holloway and Ivy Spriggs: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: That sprinkler systems are not a mandatory requirement for care homes whose occupants have either limited or no independent mobility and are therefore at higher risk from fire.
concerns.hazard: lack of mandatory sprinkler systems in care homes for limited mobility residents

concerns.quote: That care homes whose occupants have either limited or no independent mobility, and are therefore at higher risk from fire, are not deemed to be 'Higher Risk Buildings' unless they are at least 18m in height or at least 7 storeys high.
concerns.hazard: inadequate classification of higher risk buildings based on height or storeys

reports.title: Brian Harfield: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: The Government recognises that further evidence is required on the benefit of sprinklers and other additional fire protection measures in specialised housing and, to this end, we have a dedicated research workstream in place. I will consider future research findings in light of your concerns and the evidence heard at Mr [name redacted] inquest, so that we can consider what changes are necessary to reduce the risk of similar incidents in the future.
promises.summary: Research on sprinklers in specialised housing underway

concerns.quote: lack of compulsory provision for sprinklers or other fire safety measures to protect those who live at home (outside of care homes) but are being provided with extra care facilities or those in retirement type provision
concerns.hazard: lack of compulsory sprinklers in extra care facilities

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient mandatory fire protection—specifically sprinkler systems—for vulnerable older adults living outside traditional care settings.
